## Data Prep

```{r}
# Load main dataset
df2 <- read_rds(here("Data", "df2.RDS")) 

# Define rich destination countries subset
rich <- c("AUT", "BEL", "CHE", "DEU", "ESP", "FIN", "FRA", "GBR", "IRL", "ITA", "NOR", "PRT", "SWE", "JPN", "CAN", "USA", "AUS", "NZL")

# Filter, create education dummies, and calculate subset-specific within/between variables
df2_sub <- df2 %>%
  filter(iso3c %in% rich) %>%
  filter(ed_currently != 1) %>%
  mutate(
    ed3_secondary = as.integer(ed3 == 2 | ed3 == 1),
    ed3_tertiary  = as.integer(ed3 == 3)
  )

df2_sub <- df2_sub %>%
  group_by(iso3c) %>%
  mutate(
    male = ifelse(female == 1, 0, 1),
    NFE12_between = sum(SPFWT0 * NFE12, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(NFE12)], na.rm = TRUE),
    female_between = sum(SPFWT0 * female, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(female)], na.rm = TRUE),
    male_between = sum(SPFWT0 * male, na.rm = T) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(male)], na.rm = TRUE),
    children_between = sum(SPFWT0 * children, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(children)], na.rm = TRUE),
    ed3_secondary_between = sum(SPFWT0 * ed3_secondary, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(ed3_secondary)], na.rm = TRUE),
    ed3_tertiary_between  = sum(SPFWT0 * ed3_tertiary,  na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(ed3_tertiary)],  na.rm = TRUE),
    forborn_between = sum(SPFWT0 * FORBORN, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(FORBORN)], na.rm = TRUE),
    forlang_between = sum(SPFWT0 * FORLANG, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(FORLANG)], na.rm = TRUE),

    NFE12_within = NFE12 - NFE12_between,
    children_within = children - children_between,
    female_within = female - female_between,
    ed3_secondary_within = ed3_secondary - ed3_secondary_between,
    ed3_tertiary_within = ed3_tertiary - ed3_tertiary_between,
    forborn_within = FORBORN - forborn_between,
    forlang_within = FORLANG - forlang_between
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Standardize between-country effects 
between_vars <- c("NFE12_between", "female_between", "children_between", 
                  "ed3_secondary_between", "ed3_tertiary_between", 
                  "forborn_between", "forlang_between")

country_between_scaled <- function(dat, between_vars, suffix = "_z") {
  dat %>%
    distinct(iso3c, across(all_of(between_vars))) %>%
    mutate(across(all_of(between_vars), ~{
        m <- mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
        s <- sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
        if (is.na(s) || s == 0) NA_real_ else as.numeric((.x - m) / s)
      }, .names = paste0("{.col}", suffix))) %>%
    select(iso3c, ends_with(suffix))
}

df2_sub <- df2_sub %>% left_join(country_between_scaled(df2_sub, between_vars), by = "iso3c")

# Base dataframe for predictions (complete cases only)
df2r <- subset(df2_sub, !is.na(female) & !is.na(NFE12) & !is.na(children_within) & 
                 !is.na(forborn_within) & !is.na(forlang_within) & !is.na(ed3) & 
                 !is.na(skill_reading))

# Grand means for recentering
gm_female <- mean(df2r$female_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_forborn <- mean(df2r$forborn_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_children <- mean(df2r$children_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_forlang <- mean(df2r$forlang_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_nfe12 <- mean(df2r$NFE12_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_ed3_sec <- mean(df2r$ed3_secondary_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_ed3_tert <- mean(df2r$ed3_tertiary_between, na.rm = TRUE)
```

## M4 - Rich Countries

```{r}
m4_sub <- lmer(
  skill_reading ~ 
    NFE12_within + NFE12_between_z +
    female_within + female_between_z + 
    children_within + children_between_z +
    forlang_within + forlang_between_z +
    forborn_within + forborn_between_z +
    female_within * forborn_within * children_within * forlang_within * NFE12_within +
    ed3_secondary_within + ed3_secondary_between_z +
    ed3_tertiary_within + ed3_tertiary_between_z +
    (1 | iso3c),
  data = df2_sub
)

export_summs(m4_sub, statistics = "all", error_pos = "right", error_format = "({std.error})", 
             to.file = "docx", file.name = here("Results", "TS3.docx"))
```

## M5 - Rich Countries

### GLM

```{r}
m5_sub <- lmer(
  skill_reading ~ 
    NFE12_within + NFE12_between_z +
    female_within + female_between_z + 
    children_within + children_between_z +
    forlang_within + forlang_between_z +
    forborn_within + forborn_between_z +
    ed3_secondary_within + ed3_secondary_between_z +
    ed3_tertiary_within + ed3_tertiary_between_z +
    female_within * forborn_within * children_within * forlang_within * NFE12_within * ed3_tertiary_within +
    (1 | iso3c),
  data = df2_sub
)

export_summs(m5_sub, statistics = "all", error_pos = "right", error_format = "({std.error})", 
             to.file = "docx", file.name = here("Results", "TS4.docx"))
```

### ATEs

```{r}
# Function to calculate ATE from m5
calc_ate_m5 <- function(is_female, is_forborn, is_child, is_forlang, is_tertiary) {
  
  is_secondary <- ifelse(is_tertiary == 1, 0, 1)
  
  base_df <- df2r %>% mutate(
    female_within = is_female - gm_female,
    forborn_within = is_forborn - gm_forborn,
    children_within = is_child - gm_children,
    forlang_within = is_forlang - gm_forlang,
    ed3_tertiary_within = is_tertiary - gm_ed3_tert,
    ed3_secondary_within = is_secondary - gm_ed3_sec
  )
  
  df_0 <- base_df %>% mutate(NFE12_within = 0 - gm_nfe12)
  df_1 <- base_df %>% mutate(NFE12_within = 1 - gm_nfe12)
  
  pred0 <- predict(m5_sub, newdata = df_0, re.form = NA)
  pred1 <- predict(m5_sub, newdata = df_1, re.form = NA)
  
  tt <- t.test(pred1, pred0, paired = FALSE)
  
  tibble(
    AME = mean(pred1 - pred0),
    lower = tt$conf.int[1],
    upper = tt$conf.int[2]
  )
}

# Function to calculate ATE from m5
calc_ate_m5 <- function(is_female, is_forborn, is_child, is_forlang, is_tertiary) {
  
  is_secondary <- ifelse(is_tertiary == 1, 0, 1)
  
  base_df <- df2r %>% mutate(
    female_within = is_female - gm_female,
    forborn_within = is_forborn - gm_forborn,
    children_within = is_child - gm_children,
    forlang_within = is_forlang - gm_forlang,
    ed3_tertiary_within = is_tertiary - gm_ed3_tert,
    ed3_secondary_within = is_secondary - gm_ed3_sec
  )
  
  df_0 <- base_df %>% mutate(NFE12_within = 0 - gm_nfe12)
  df_1 <- base_df %>% mutate(NFE12_within = 1 - gm_nfe12)
  
  pred0 <- predict(m5_sub, newdata = df_0, re.form = NA)
  pred1 <- predict(m5_sub, newdata = df_1, re.form = NA)
  
  tt <- t.test(pred1, pred0, paired = FALSE)
  
  tibble(
    AME = mean(pred1 - pred0),
    lower = tt$conf.int[1],
    upper = tt$conf.int[2]
  )
}

# The 12 Intersectional Profiles
profiles <- tribble(
  ~type_id, ~type_label, ~is_female, ~is_forborn, ~is_child, ~is_forlang,
  "1f", "1f. Foreign-born mother\nnon-native speaker", 1, 1, 1, 1,
  "2f", "2f. Foreign-born no children female\nnon-native speaker", 1, 1, 0, 1,
  "3f", "3f. Foreign-born mother\nnative speaker", 1, 1, 1, 0,
  "4f", "4f. Foreign-born no children female\nnative speaker", 1, 1, 0, 0,
  "5f", "5f. Native-born mother\nnative speaker", 1, 0, 1, 0,
  "6f", "6f. Native-born no children female\nnative speaker", 1, 0, 0, 0,
  "1m", "1m. Foreign-born father\nnon-native speaker", 0, 1, 1, 1,
  "2m", "2m. Foreign-born no children male\nnon-native speaker", 0, 1, 0, 1,
  "3m", "3m. Foreign-born father\nnative speaker", 0, 1, 1, 0,
  "4m", "4m. Foreign-born no children male\nnative speaker", 0, 1, 0, 0,
  "5m", "5m. Native-born father\nnative speaker", 0, 0, 1, 0,
  "6m", "6m. Native-born no children male\nnative speaker", 0, 0, 0, 0
)

# Compute ATEs
ame_m5_sub <- crossing(
  profiles,
  is_tertiary = c(0, 1)
) %>%
  mutate(
    res = pmap(list(is_female, is_forborn, is_child, is_forlang, is_tertiary), calc_ate_m5)
  ) %>%
  unnest(res)
```

### Build Fig S6. M5 ATEs

Must be very careful here... The differences between m5 and m5_sub are a combination:

True contextual differences: The causal effect of ALE genuinely differs when the labor market and educational infrastructure belong to a high-income destination country.

Distributional reality: The mathematical "average" citizen (the baseline gm_ zero-point) is fundamentally different in the rich subset.

For the purposes of a global ATE, I only want the true ATE (for rich countries). Therefore, I run a counterfactual below to check if this is more of a context or composition effect (ATes in rich v all countries in sample)

```{r}
# Prepare Metadata and Styling
ame_m5_sub <- ame_m5_sub %>%
  mutate(
    ed_label = ifelse(is_tertiary == 1, "Tertiary", "Non-Tertiary"),
    idx = as.integer(substr(type_id, 1, 1)),
    sex = substr(type_id, 2, 2)
  )

type_order_sub <- ame_m5_sub %>% distinct(type_label, idx, sex) %>% arrange(idx, sex) %>% pull(type_label)
ame_m5_sub$type_label <- factor(ame_m5_sub$type_label, levels = rev(type_order_sub))

ame_m5_sub <- ame_m5_sub %>%
  mutate(
    Female = ifelse(sex == "f", 1, 0),
    `Foreign-born` = ifelse(is_forborn == 1, 1, 0),
    `Non-native-speaker` = ifelse(is_forlang == 1, 1, 0),
    Parent = ifelse(is_child == 1, 1, 0)
  )

pal12_sub <- viridis(n = nlevels(ame_m5_sub$type_label), option = "D", begin = 0.1, end = 0.9)


dot_df_sub <- ame_m5_sub %>%
  filter(is_tertiary == 0) %>%
  select(type_label, Female, `Foreign-born`, `Non-native-speaker`, Parent) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Female, `Foreign-born`, `Non-native-speaker`, Parent), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = c("Female", "Foreign-born", "Non-native-speaker", "Parent")))

p_dots_sub <- ggplot(dot_df_sub, aes(x = variable, y = type_label)) +
  geom_point(data = subset(dot_df_sub, value == 0), shape = 21, size = 3.2, stroke = 0.5, fill = "white", color = "black") +
  geom_point(data = subset(dot_df_sub, value == 1), shape = 16, size = 3.2, color = "black") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Non-Tertiary
p_bar_sub <- ggplot(subset(ame_m5_sub, is_tertiary == 0), aes(x = type_label, y = AME, fill = type_label)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.55, color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.15) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal12_sub) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-10, 40, by = 5)) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(-1, 35)) + 
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Non-Tertiary\nEducation (Rich)") + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "none")

#Tertiary 
p_bar_t_sub <- ggplot(subset(ame_m5_sub, is_tertiary == 1), aes(x = type_label, y = AME, fill = type_label)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.55, color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.15) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal12_sub) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-10, 40, by = 5)) + 
  coord_flip(ylim = c(-1, 35)) + 
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Tertiary Education\n(Rich)") + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "none")


diff_df_sub <- ame_m5_sub %>%
  select(type_label, is_tertiary, AME) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = is_tertiary, values_from = AME, names_prefix = "tert_") %>%
  mutate(
    diff = tert_0 - tert_1,
    diff_label = sprintf("%+.0f", round(diff)) 
  )

p_diff_sub <- ggplot(diff_df_sub, aes(x = type_label, y = 0)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = diff_label), size = 4, fontface = "bold", color = "grey30", hjust = 0) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "AME\nDifference") + 
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),           
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),          
    panel.grid = element_blank(),          
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),        
    axis.title.x = element_text(color = "grey30", size = 9, face = "bold.italic", hjust = 0)
```

## Counterfactual - checking context v composition in ATEs

Predict out of sample to the entire set of countries using the ATEs from only the rich countries. Check difference to understand how much are compositional differences.

```{r}
### Counterfactual: Rich Slopes applied to Global Baseline

# preserving natural variance in global dataset
df2_global <- df2 %>%
  filter(ed_currently != 1) %>%
  mutate(
    ed3_secondary = as.integer(ed3 == 2 | ed3 == 1),
    ed3_tertiary  = as.integer(ed3 == 3)
  ) %>%
  group_by(iso3c) %>%
  mutate(
    NFE12_between = sum(SPFWT0 * NFE12, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(NFE12)], na.rm = TRUE),
    female_between = sum(SPFWT0 * female, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(female)], na.rm = TRUE),
    children_between = sum(SPFWT0 * children, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(children)], na.rm = TRUE),
    ed3_secondary_between = sum(SPFWT0 * ed3_secondary, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(ed3_secondary)], na.rm = TRUE),
    ed3_tertiary_between  = sum(SPFWT0 * ed3_tertiary,  na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(ed3_tertiary)],  na.rm = TRUE),
    forborn_between = sum(SPFWT0 * FORBORN, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(FORBORN)], na.rm = TRUE),
    forlang_between = sum(SPFWT0 * FORLANG, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(FORLANG)], na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Apply z-scoring to global between-effects
df2_global <- df2_global %>% left_join(country_between_scaled(df2_global, between_vars), by = "iso3c")

# Filter to complete cases for predictions
df2r_global <- subset(df2_global, !is.na(female) & !is.na(NFE12) & !is.na(children) & 
                 !is.na(FORBORN) & !is.na(FORLANG) & !is.na(ed3) & 
                 !is.na(skill_reading))

# Calculate global grand means
gm_female_global <- mean(df2r_global$female_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_forborn_global <- mean(df2r_global$forborn_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_children_global <- mean(df2r_global$children_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_forlang_global <- mean(df2r_global$forlang_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_nfe12_global <- mean(df2r_global$NFE12_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_ed3_sec_global <- mean(df2r_global$ed3_secondary_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_ed3_tert_global <- mean(df2r_global$ed3_tertiary_between, na.rm = TRUE)


# Counterfactual Prediction Function
calc_ate_cf <- function(is_female, is_forborn, is_child, is_forlang, is_tertiary) {
  
  is_secondary <- ifelse(is_tertiary == 1, 0, 1)
  
  # Apply global grand means to the target specification
  base_df <- df2r_global %>% mutate(
    female_within = is_female - gm_female_global,
    forborn_within = is_forborn - gm_forborn_global,
    children_within = is_child - gm_children_global,
    forlang_within = is_forlang - gm_forlang_global,
    ed3_tertiary_within = is_tertiary - gm_ed3_tert_global,
    ed3_secondary_within = is_secondary - gm_ed3_sec_global
  )
  
  df_0 <- base_df %>% mutate(NFE12_within = 0 - gm_nfe12_global)
  df_1 <- base_df %>% mutate(NFE12_within = 1 - gm_nfe12_global)
  
  # Predict using m5_sub (Rich Slopes) on global counterfactual data
  pred0 <- predict(m5_sub, newdata = df_0, re.form = NA)
  pred1 <- predict(m5_sub, newdata = df_1, re.form = NA)
  
  tt <- t.test(pred1, pred0, paired = FALSE)
  
  tibble(
    AME_cf = mean(pred1 - pred0),
    lower_cf = tt$conf.int[1],
    upper_cf = tt$conf.int[2]
  )
}

#Counterfactual ATEs
ame_cf <- crossing(
  profiles,
  is_tertiary = c(0, 1)
) %>%
  mutate(
    res = pmap(list(is_female, is_forborn, is_child, is_forlang, is_tertiary), calc_ate_cf)
  ) %>%
  unnest(res)

ame_comparison <- ame_m5_sub %>%
  select(type_id, type_label, is_tertiary, AME_Rich = AME) %>%
  left_join(
    ame_cf %>% select(type_id, is_tertiary, AME_cf),
    by = c("type_id", "is_tertiary")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Education = ifelse(is_tertiary == 1, "Tertiary", "Non-Tertiary"),
    Difference = AME_cf - AME_Rich
  ) %>%
  select(type_id, type_label, Education, AME_Rich, AME_cf, Difference) %>%
  arrange(desc(Education), type_id)

kable(ame_comparison, digits = 2, 
      col.names = c("ID", "Profile", "Education", "AME (Rich Data)", "AME (Global Data)", "Diff (Compositional Shift)"),
      caption = "Comparing Structural Rich-Country Effects on Rich vs. Global Populations") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"))
```

The results show that composition has little to do with it. When exptrapolating to the middle-income 10 country sample, the ATEs change almost none. This means that differences observed in the models are likely due to true contextual differences in the causal effect of ALE, rather than just compositional differences in the baseline characteristics of the populations. This means that intersectionality is not universal in returns to human capital, but carries some contextual specificities. This should already have been clear theoreically when taking an approach initially designed to integrate race, as it plays out in the North American context, into a global context where it is necessary to discuss 'otherness' or 'foreignness' because many are treated severley as outsiders who have essentially 'white' skin and appear pheontypically similar.

## M5 - Middle-income Countries

### Prep

```{r}
## Middle-Income Countries Check (Inverse of Rich)

### Data Prep (Middle-Income)

# Filter for middle-income countries
df2_mid <- df2 %>%
  filter(!iso3c %in% rich) %>%
  filter(ed_currently != 1) %>%
  mutate(
    ed3_secondary = as.integer(ed3 == 2 | ed3 == 1),
    ed3_tertiary  = as.integer(ed3 == 3)
  )

# Calculate subset-specific within/between variables
df2_mid <- df2_mid %>%
  group_by(iso3c) %>%
  mutate(
    male = ifelse(female == 1, 0, 1),
    NFE12_between = sum(SPFWT0 * NFE12, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(NFE12)], na.rm = TRUE),
    female_between = sum(SPFWT0 * female, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(female)], na.rm = TRUE),
    male_between = sum(SPFWT0 * male, na.rm = T) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(male)], na.rm = TRUE),
    children_between = sum(SPFWT0 * children, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(children)], na.rm = TRUE),
    ed3_secondary_between = sum(SPFWT0 * ed3_secondary, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(ed3_secondary)], na.rm = TRUE),
    ed3_tertiary_between  = sum(SPFWT0 * ed3_tertiary,  na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(ed3_tertiary)],  na.rm = TRUE),
    forborn_between = sum(SPFWT0 * FORBORN, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(FORBORN)], na.rm = TRUE),
    forlang_between = sum(SPFWT0 * FORLANG, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(SPFWT0[!is.na(FORLANG)], na.rm = TRUE),

    NFE12_within = NFE12 - NFE12_between,
    children_within = children - children_between,
    female_within = female - female_between,
    ed3_secondary_within = ed3_secondary - ed3_secondary_between,
    ed3_tertiary_within = ed3_tertiary - ed3_tertiary_between,
    forborn_within = FORBORN - forborn_between,
    forlang_within = FORLANG - forlang_between
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Standardize between-country effects
df2_mid <- df2_mid %>% left_join(country_between_scaled(df2_mid, between_vars), by = "iso3c")

# Base dataframe for predictions
df2r_mid <- subset(df2_mid, !is.na(female) & !is.na(NFE12) & !is.na(children_within) & 
                 !is.na(forborn_within) & !is.na(forlang_within) & !is.na(ed3) & 
                 !is.na(skill_reading))

# Grand means for recentering
gm_female_mid <- mean(df2r_mid$female_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_forborn_mid <- mean(df2r_mid$forborn_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_children_mid <- mean(df2r_mid$children_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_forlang_mid <- mean(df2r_mid$forlang_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_nfe12_mid <- mean(df2r_mid$NFE12_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_ed3_sec_mid <- mean(df2r_mid$ed3_secondary_between, na.rm = TRUE)
gm_ed3_tert_mid <- mean(df2r_mid$ed3_tertiary_between, na.rm = TRUE)


m5_mid <- lmer(
  skill_reading ~ 
    NFE12_within + NFE12_between_z +
    female_within + female_between_z + 
    children_within + children_between_z +
    forlang_within + forlang_between_z +
    forborn_within + forborn_between_z +
    ed3_secondary_within + ed3_secondary_between_z +
    ed3_tertiary_within + ed3_tertiary_between_z +
    female_within * forborn_within * children_within * forlang_within * NFE12_within * ed3_tertiary_within +
    (1 | iso3c),
  data = df2_mid
)

export_summs(m5_mid, statistics = "all", error_pos = "right", error_format = "({std.error})", 
             to.file = "docx", file.name = here("Results", "TS5_MiddleIncome.docx"))
```

### ATEs

```{r}
# Function to calculate ATE from m5_mid
calc_ate_m5_mid <- function(is_female, is_forborn, is_child, is_forlang, is_tertiary) {
  
  is_secondary <- ifelse(is_tertiary == 1, 0, 1)
  
  base_df <- df2r_mid %>% mutate(
    female_within = is_female - gm_female_mid,
    forborn_within = is_forborn - gm_forborn_mid,
    children_within = is_child - gm_children_mid,
    forlang_within = is_forlang - gm_forlang_mid,
    ed3_tertiary_within = is_tertiary - gm_ed3_tert_mid,
    ed3_secondary_within = is_secondary - gm_ed3_sec_mid
  )
  
  df_0 <- base_df %>% mutate(NFE12_within = 0 - gm_nfe12_mid)
  df_1 <- base_df %>% mutate(NFE12_within = 1 - gm_nfe12_mid)
  
  pred0 <- predict(m5_mid, newdata = df_0, re.form = NA)
  pred1 <- predict(m5_mid, newdata = df_1, re.form = NA)
  
  tt <- t.test(pred1, pred0, paired = FALSE)
  
  tibble(
    AME = mean(pred1 - pred0),
    lower = tt$conf.int[1],
    upper = tt$conf.int[2]
  )
}

# Compute ATEs
ame_m5_mid <- crossing(
  profiles,
  is_tertiary = c(0, 1)
) %>%
  mutate(
    res = pmap(list(is_female, is_forborn, is_child, is_forlang, is_tertiary), calc_ate_m5_mid)
  ) %>%
  unnest(res)
```

## Country-By-Country Models

### Loop across

```{r}

## Country-By-Country Models

all_countries <- unique(df2$iso3c)

df2_valid_loop <- df2 %>%
  filter(ed_currently != 1) %>% 
  mutate(ed3_tertiary = as.integer(ed3 == 3)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(female) & !is.na(FORBORN) & !is.na(children) & 
         !is.na(FORLANG) & !is.na(NFE12) & !is.na(ed3_tertiary) & 
         !is.na(skill_reading) & !is.na(SPFWT0))

# Setup raw grid for predictions
pred_grid_raw <- crossing(
  profiles,
  is_tertiary = c(0, 1)
) %>%
  rename(
    female = is_female,
    FORBORN = is_forborn,
    children = is_child,
    FORLANG = is_forlang,
    ed3_tertiary = is_tertiary
  )

# Extract ATE per country across ALL countries
country_ates <- map_dfr(all_countries, function(c_code) {
  
  df_c <- df2_valid_loop %>% filter(iso3c == c_code)
  
  # Ensure sufficient observations for intersectional model
  if(nrow(df_c) < 50) return(NULL)
  
  # Run unadjusted OLS 
  m_c <- lm(skill_reading ~ female * FORBORN * children * FORLANG * NFE12 * ed3_tertiary, 
            data = df_c, weights = SPFWT0)
  
  grid_0 <- pred_grid_raw %>% mutate(NFE12 = 0)
  grid_1 <- pred_grid_raw %>% mutate(NFE12 = 1)
  
  # Predict handling rank deficiency 
  p0 <- tryCatch(predict(m_c, newdata = grid_0), error = function(e) rep(NA, nrow(grid_0)))
  p1 <- tryCatch(predict(m_c, newdata = grid_1), error = function(e) rep(NA, nrow(grid_1)))
  
  pred_grid_raw %>%
    mutate(
      iso3c = c_code,
      AME = p1 - p0
    )
})

# Helper to drop min and max for trimmed means
trim_vec <- function(x) {
  x <- na.omit(x)
  if(length(x) <= 2) return(x) # Prevents error if country counts fall too low
  sort(x)[-c(1, length(x))]
}

# Aggregate cross-country ATEs and calculate 95% CIs
country_summary <- country_ates %>%
  group_by(type_id, type_label, female, FORBORN, children, FORLANG, ed3_tertiary) %>%
  summarise(
    # Standard 
    AME_mean = mean(AME, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_AME = sd(AME, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_countries = sum(!is.na(AME)),
    # Trimmed (Drops min and max)
    AME_mean_trim = mean(trim_vec(AME)),
    sd_AME_trim = sd(trim_vec(AME)),
    n_countries_trim = length(trim_vec(AME)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Standard Errors & CIs
    se = sd_AME / sqrt(n_countries),
    lower = AME_mean - qt(0.975, n_countries - 1) * se,
    upper = AME_mean + qt(0.975, n_countries - 1) * se,
    
    # Trimmed Errors & CIs
    se_trim = sd_AME_trim / sqrt(n_countries_trim),
    lower_trim = AME_mean_trim - qt(0.975, n_countries_trim - 1) * se_trim,
    upper_trim = AME_mean_trim + qt(0.975, n_countries_trim - 1) * se_trim
  )

# Add visualization meta-labels
country_summary <- country_summary %>%
  mutate(
    ed_label = ifelse(ed3_tertiary == 1, "Tertiary", "Non-Tertiary"),
    idx = as.integer(substr(type_id, 1, 1)),
    sex = substr(type_id, 2, 2),
    # Map raw 1/0 flags for Dot Matrix plot
    Female = female,
    `Foreign-born` = FORBORN,
    `Non-native-speaker` = FORLANG,
    Parent = children
  )

# Enforce uniform factor ordering
type_order_c <- country_summary %>% distinct(type_label, idx, sex) %>% arrange(idx, sex) %>% pull(type_label)
country_summary$type_label <- factor(country_summary$type_label, levels = rev(type_order_c))
```
